paragraphs: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel. He challenged Rav Yosef, Ketubbot 36b:15. He is ‘the judges of Pumbedita’ (see there). An old slave dyed his beard black so that he would look young. He came to Rava, who did not buy him; Rav Pappa bar Shmuel bought him. The slave washed his beard and said, ‘I am older than your father.’ Rav Pappa applied to himself: ‘The righteous man’—Rava—‘is delivered from trouble, and another comes in his place’; end of Ha-Zahav. He established a measure, and they called it ‘roz Pappa’: Bava Batra 90b; see Arukh, entry רז. In Shabbat 54b he sat before Rav Hisda (Maharshal's reading is Nahman), and said, etc.; Rav Nahman said to him. In Bava Batra 73b, Rabbah bar bar Hana said: ‘I myself saw that frog, which was as large as sixty houses. A serpent came,’ etc. Rav Pappa bar Shmuel said, ‘Had I not been there, I would not have believed it.’ Rava spoke to him: Rosh Hashanah 27a, 34b:9 [Heilprin’s side indicator is יב]; Bava Metzia 109, beginning of b. Rav Shmuel bar Pappa may be his son, named for his grandfather. Yuhasin writes that Shmuel, Rav's colleague, had a son called Rav Pappa; perhaps this is he. But Shmuel was a priest. See R' Abba bar Pappa the priest.
